Collective Worship in School
We use Roots and Fruits as a Christian Collective Worship resource over a two-year period. Rooted in Bible teaching, there are 12 Christian Values which we focus on one per half-term. The values link with the season of the Church year. We use Roots and Fruits as a Christian Collective Worship resource over a three-year period – you can see the rolling program below. Rooted in Bible teaching, there are 12 Christian Values which we focus on one per half-term. The values link with the season of the Church year.
We invite parents to continue the theme for each half-term at home using our Home School Values. Please do have a look, dip in and use the sheets to have fun, stimulate discussion and reflect. The key is to do it together!

pageCache.pageTitle: Chilthorne Domer Church School - Sport Premium
pageCache.text:
Sport Premium
The Sports Premium is designed to help primary schools improve the quality of the PE and sport activities they offer their pupils. Schools receive funding to improve the quality of the PE and sport activities they offer their pupils, and are free to choose the best way of using the money. This funding is provided jointly by the Departments for Education, Health and Culture, Media and Sport and can only be spent on the provision of PE and sport in schools.
The School Games Mark is a government-led awards scheme launched in 2012 to reward schools for their commitment to the development of competition across their school and into the community. We are proud holders of The Platinum Mark, the highest Mark achievable, awarded to schools that have met the standard for the Gold Mark in the previous four years.
Please see our latest update on what is happening with the sports premium money by downloading the PDF files linked from this section. This information is inline with the new DfE funding criteria, referencing the 5 key indicators.

Admissions and new starters
Many of the pages you will need are linked from the 'In this section' part of this page (either to your left on a PC or at the bottom of the page on a mobile device) including:
Choosing the right school for your child is one of the most important decisions you'll make in their early lives. We understand how important it is, and we are pleased to be able to offer school tours. The tour dates for 2027 starters are below but do get in touch via the office if you have any questions in the meantime. 01935 840407 or office@cdcs.uk.
We are offering Stay and Play sessions in the autumn for you and your child to immerse yourselves in our school life. Details can be found below. You are also warmly invited to our open-day where you will be able to tour the school and speak to some of our wonderful children and staff. This will take place on Wednesday 14th October 2026. Please book your places for any of the above by contacting the school office.
Mrs Chesterton is usually available at the end of the phone and is happy to chat with any prospective parents – please just phone the school office to make an appointment.
The wonderful Towers Wills Estate Agent in Yeovil spent some time filming our school day. Click on the video in the 'In this section' to see our school in action.

Residential trips
Children get the opportunity to take part in two residential trips during their time at Chilthorne Domer.
Children in year 4 get to visit a PGL activity centre and experience their first taste of being away from home with their friends. Our next trip is April 2027.
Upper key stage two children will have this opportunity to visit London in either year 5 or year 6. Our trips fall on even years. This trip is 3 days and 2 nights and children get to experience lots of what our capital city has to offer, including the zoo, museums, a river cruise, the London Eye and even a West End show!
Our next trip will be in June 2028.

pageCache.pageTitle: Chilthorne Domer Church School - Our curriculum
pageCache.text:
Our curriculum
The ultimate vision for our curriculum is to provide children with opportunities to: experience memorable and enchanting moments, foster positive relationships; gain an understanding of the importance of mental health and wellbeing; develop a greater understanding and knowledge of the world around them; develop curiosity, enquire and ask questions through philosophical enquiry; nurture and grow their aspirations and equip them with the knowledge, skills and confidence needed for a 21st century world.
At Chilthorne Domer, we teach a carefully sequenced, knowledge-rich curriculum which aims to inspire pupils and promote excellent outcomes for all. We want children to become experts in their subjects – to become historians, geographers, artists to name a few, so we organise our curriculum into 3 terms; Discover, Explore and Create. This gives the children the opportunity to fully focus and immerse themselves in their learning journey.
The curriculum content has been carefully chosen by our own subject experts, alongside the National Curriculum, and is organised in a coherent way, ensuring children can build on their knowledge from year to year. In this way, the knowledge in the curriculum is cumulative, constructing firm foundations and schema from which children can progress and develop deeper conceptual understanding and subject-specific knowledge and skills over time.
Curriculum coherence ensures that teaching does not jump from topic to topic, but enables children to develop knowledge over time, as well as a love of subjects. Subject content is crucial to this approach – the rich content of the curriculum inspires children and plants the seeds for a lifetime of learning. Lessons are taught with talk and thinking critically at the heart. Children are encouraged to learn in a variety of ways.
To find out more about our school curriculum, please follow the links to each subject. If you need further information, please contact the office and they will put you in touch with the relevant subject lead.

SEND
Chilthorne Domer Church School is an inclusive school, where all children are supported to achieve their very best. 'Together we love, we aim high and we celebrate!' is our mission statement for all pupils within our school, including those with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities.
We are committed to supporting all pupils with needs in all 4 areas as set out in the SEN Code of Practice: Cognition and Learning, Communication and Interaction, Social Emotional and Mental Health and Sensory and/or Physical Needs.
Special Educational Needs and Disabilities Coordinator:
Our Inclusion Lead and Special educational needs and disabilities coordinator is Mrs Chloe Cahill
Mrs Cahill's working days are Mondays and Tuesdays and she can be contacted via the school Office on 01935 840407. Please do make contact if you would like to arrange a conversation or visit with her to discuss your child's individual needs.
